conventions.convention: Disk-embedding data use finite signed equivariant intersection sums with chosen whiskers. Wall's unreduced self-intersection sum identifies a group element with its inverse. A prescribed disk-boundary framing need not extend; its relative Euler obstruction is separate.

Goodness quantifies over every based disk-like height-1.5 capped grope and every homomorphism from its actual four-dimensional neighborhood group. The output is a framed immersed disk whose double-point loops map to the identity.

The tower construction assumes Countable Choice and a supplied compatible smooth neighborhood, smooth maps, collars and framings. It does not assert that an arbitrary topological neighborhood admits a smoothing.
S-equivalence uses integral unimodular congruences and the displayed symmetric-coupling tube enlargement or its inverse. The empty form is represented by the zero-by-zero matrix.
With positive-push entries V_ij = lk(a_i^+,a_j), reflecting and reversing the surface orientation gives the reverse-mirror matrix −V in the image basis; reflection alone gives the negative transpose.

The Alexander-one theorem assumes full AC, takes smooth oriented knots as input, and asserts a locally flat proper disk in the standard four-ball. Alexander polynomials are compared up to Laurent units ±t^k.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. In the stated supplied smooth neighborhood V with good fundamental group, finite proper smooth generic disk data with pairwise disjoint embedded framed boundaries and framed smooth immersed dual spheres satisfying the listed equivariant intersection and self-intersection conditions yield disjoint proper locally flat disks homotopic to the original disks rel boundary and framing, with constructed product normal neighborhoods and framed immersed geometric duals homotopic to the original spheres.

Under full AC, a smooth oriented Alexander-one knot supplies the stated geometric zero-long-block Seifert basis, a marked smooth surface in the literal radius-3/2 ball with infinite-cyclic complement group, and framed smooth compression disks and dual spheres satisfying all the displayed Wall conditions, with compression-compatible attaching annuli and framings. For genus zero the families are empty.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The infinite cyclic group Z is good for the Freedman disk-embedding theorem, in the sense of the π1-null disk property defined for a good fundamental group.

Under full AC, for every Seifert surface of a smooth oriented knot with Alexander polynomial equal to one up to a Laurent unit, every positive-push integral Seifert matrix represents a form S-equivalent over Z to the empty form.

Under full AC, a smooth oriented Alexander-one knot has a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface with the stated geometric symplectic basis and Seifert matrix [[0,I+U],[U^T,W]], where U is strictly upper triangular and W is symmetric with zero diagonal.

Assume full AC. If a smooth oriented knot K in S^3 has Alexander polynomial equal to one up to a unit ±t^k, then there is a locally flat proper embedding D^2 into B^4 whose boundary is K. The conclusion asserts no smooth slice disk.
